({{IPAc-en|'|j|ou|n|ə|s|}} {{IPAc-en|ˌ|v|ae|l|ə|n|'|tʃ|u|n|ə|s|}} {{respell|YOH|nəss}} {{respell|VAL|ən|CHOO|nəs}}; {{IPA|lt|ˈjoːnɐs vɐɫɐnʲˈtɕûːnɐs}}; born 6 May 1992) is a Lithuanian professional [[basketball]] player for [[BC Žalgiris|Žalgiris]] of the [[Lietuvos krepšinio lyga|Lithuanian Basketball League]] (LKL) and the [[EuroLeague]]. He was selected by the [[Toronto Raptors]] with the fifth overall pick in the [[2011 NBA draft]]. He has also played for the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], [[New Orleans Pelicans]], [[Washington Wizards]], [[Sacramento Kings]], and [[Denver Nuggets]]. Valančiūnas has been a member of the [[Lithuania men's national basketball team|Lithuania national team]] since age 19. He won two [[EuroBasket]] silver medals in [[EuroBasket 2013]] and [[EuroBasket 2015]], earning [[EuroBasket All-Tournament Team|All-Tournament honours]] in the latter. Valančiūnas also appeared in the documentary ''[[The Other Dream Team]]''. ==Professional career== ===Perlas (2008–2010)=== Valančiūnas started playing professionally for [[BC Perlas|Perlas]] in 2008. During the 2008–09 season the team played in the [[National Basketball League (Lithuania)|National Basketball League]] (NKL), Lithuania's second strongest league, but moved up to the top-tier [[Lithuanian Basketball League]] (LKL) the following season. In January 2009 Valančiūnas signed a long-term contract with [[BC Lietuvos rytas|Lietuvos rytas]], but, as Perlas was Lietuvos rytas' farm club, he did not immediately move to Lietuvos rytas, staying with Perlas for the first half of the 2009–10 season.{{cite web |title=Dainys ir Valančiūnas – "Lietuvos ryto" nariai |url=https://www.basketnews.lt/news-19624-dainys-ir-valanciunas-lietuvos-ryto-nariai.html |website=basketnews.lt |access-date=25 June 2020 |language=lt-LT |date=15 January 2009}} ===Lietuvos rytas (2010–2012)=== On 17 January 2010, Valančiūnas finally moved to Lietuvos rytas. A month after that Lietuvos rytas won the 2010 edition of [[Lithuanian Basketball Federation]]'s [[LKF Cup]]. While playing there, Valančiūnas played in the [[LKL Finals]] three times, in 2010, 2011 and 2012. The team won the 2010 series 4–3 against [[BC Žalgiris|Žalgiris]], but lost to the same team the following year 4–1 and 3–0 in 2012. Valančiūnas became February's MVP in the [[VTB United League]] in 2012.{{cite web |title=Jonas Valanciunas - is MVP of February |url=http://www.vtb-league.com/en/news/yonas-valanchyunas---mvp-fevralya.htm |website=vtb-league.com |access-date=25 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131019102648/http://www.vtb-league.com/en/news/yonas-valanchyunas---mvp-fevralya.htm |archive-date=19 October 2013 |date=2 March 2012}} Two months later he won the [[EuroCup Rising Star]] award and was named in the [[EuroCup Basketball All-EuroCup Team|All-EuroCup squad]]. He averaged 10.8 points, 7.6 rebounds and 1.6 blocks, while shooting 63.4% from the field, leading Lietuvos rytas to third place. Valančiūnas participated in three [[LKL All-Star Game]]s in [[2010 LKL All-Star Game|2010]], [[2011 LKL All-Star Game|2011]] and [[2012 LKL All-Star Game|2012]]. During the 2011 All-Star Game Valančiūnas scored 18 points and grabbed 10 rebounds, helping this team win the game. He was named as the 2011 [[LKL All-Star Game Most Valuable Player Award|LKL All-Star Game MVP]]. During the 2012 game he led his team to victory, scoring 25 points including one three-pointer, grabbing 13 rebounds and dishing out 6 assists. He won the MVP award once again.{{cite web |title=LKL šventėje ryškiausiai švietė Valančiūno žvaigždė (2 video, foto, komentarai) |url=https://www.basketnews.lt/news-48254-lkl-sventeje-ryskiausiai-sviete-valanciuno-zvaigzde-2-video-foto-komentarai.html |website=basketnews.lt |access-date=25 June 2020 |language=lt-LT |date=3 March 2012}} In December 2011, Valančiūnas was named the [[Lithuanian Basketball Player of the Year]] for the first time.{{cite web |title=Geriausi 2011 metų Lietuvos krepšininkai – Jonas Valančiūnas ir Rima Valentienė |url=https://www.15min.lt/24sek/naujiena/archyvas/geriausi-2011-metu-lietuvos-krepsininkai-jonas-valanciunas-ir-rima-valentiene-872-187114 |website=15min.lt |access-date=25 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120110084007/http://www.15min.lt/naujiena/sportas/krepsinis/geriausi-2011-metu-lietuvos-krepsininkai-jonas-valanciunas-ir-rima-valentiene-23-187114 |archive-date=10 January 2012 |language=lt |date=27 December 2011}} He was also twice named the [[FIBA Europe Young Men's Player of the Year Award|FIBA European Young Player of the Year]] in February 2012 and February 2013.{{cite web |title=Valanciunas, Young Men's Player Of 2011 |url=http://www.fibaeurope.com/coid_-nQH1cdsHBkL7j4BTFAE33.articleMode_on.html |website=fibaeurope.com |access-date=25 June 2020 |date=13 February 2012}}{{cite web |title=Valanciunas Young Men's POY 2012 |url=http://www.fibaeurope.com/cid_VHACRq3SJT668RpnEPBL82.coid_MUMtgYLNGw6ts8a4RCdLp3.articleMode_on.html |website=fibaeurope.com |access-date=25 June 2020 |date=6 February 2013}} ===Toronto Raptors (2012–2019)=== ====2012–13 season==== [[File:Greg Monroe Post Shot (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|205px|Valančiūnas blocks future teammate [[Greg Monroe]] in 2013]] Valančiūnas was considered as a top prospect at the [[2011 NBA draft]], held on 23 June 2011, and was drafted fifth overall by the [[Toronto Raptors]]. He signed with the Raptors on 18 July 2012,{{cite web |title=Raptors Sign Centre Jonas Valanciunas |url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/20120718/121291/raptors-sign-centre-jonas-valanciunas |website=NBA.com |access-date=25 June 2020 |date=18 July 2012}} and made his NBA debut on 31 October, during a game against the [[Indiana Pacers]]. He recorded 12 points and 10 rebounds in 23 minutes of action as a starter, becoming the first Raptors rookie since [[Damon Stoudamire]] in 1995 to record a [[double-double]] in his first game.{{cite web |date=31 October 2012 |title=George Hill, Pacers rally past Raptors in season opener |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400277724 |access-date=25 June 2020 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}} In December 2012, Valančiūnas was selected as the Lithuanian Basketball Player of the Year for the second time.{{cite web |title=23 tūkstančiai aistruolių nusprendė: Jonas Valančiūnas ir Sandra Linkevičienė – geriausi Lietuvos krepšininkai |url=https://www.15min.lt/24sek/naujiena/archyvas/23-tukstanciai-aistruoliu-nusprende-jonas-valanciunas-ir-sandra-linkeviciene-geriausi-lietuvos-krepsininkai-872-287196 |website=15min.lt |access-date=25 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121215120119/http://www.15min.lt/naujiena/sportas/krepsinis/23-tukstanciai-aistruoliu-nusprende-jonas-valanciunas-ir-sandra-linkeviciene-geriausi-lietuvos-krepsininkai-23-287196 |archive-date=15 December 2012 |language=lt |date=11 December 2012}} On 5 April 2013, Valančiūnas was named [[Eastern Conference (NBA)|Eastern Conference]]'s Rookie of the Month for games played in March. He ranked first among Eastern Conference rookies in averages per game in rebounds (7.3), blocks (1.07), and field goal percentage (.620). He also ranked second in free throw percentage (.822) and fourth in scoring (11.4 points per game), reaching double figures in points in 11 of his last 12 games between 6 and 31 March.{{cite web |title=Raptors' Jonas Valanciunas, Trail Blazers' Damian Lillard named Kia NBA Rookies of the Month |url=https://pr.nba.com/jonas-valanciunas-damian-lillard-kia-nba-rookies-of-the-month/ |website=NBA.com |access-date=25 June 2020 |date=5 April 2013}} ====2013–14 season==== On 22 July 2013, Valančiūnas was named MVP of the [[2013 NBA Summer League|Las Vegas Summer League]] becoming the first non-American to win the award after averaging 19 points and 10 rebounds in four games.{{cite web |last1=Harper |first1=Zach |title=Jonas Valanciunas named 2013 Las Vegas Summer League MVP |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/jonas-valanciunas-named-2013-las-vegas-summer-league-mvp/ |website=CBSSports.com |access-date=25 June 2020 |date=22 July 2013}} On 27 December, Valančiūnas recorded a then career-high 18 rebounds in a 95–83 win over the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web |title=Raptors rally past Carmelo Anthony-less Knicks |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400489303 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=25 June 2020 |date=27 December 2013}} On 9 April 2014, he scored a then career-high 26 points in a 125–114 win over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web |title=Jonas Valanciunas apologizes for arrest, has career high for Raptors |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400490037 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=25 July 2026 |date=9 April 2014}} Two days later, he recorded a then career-high 21 rebounds in a 108–100 loss to the New York Knicks.{{cite web |title=Raptors secure division despite loss to Knicks - CityNews Toronto |url=https://toronto.citynews.ca/2014/04/11/raptors-secure-division-despite-loss-to-knicks/ |website=toronto.citynews.ca |access-date=25 June 2020 |date=11 April 2014}} The Raptors finished in third place in the conference in the [[2013–14 NBA season|2013–14 season]], and faced the sixth-seeded [[Brooklyn Nets]] in the first round of the [[2014 NBA playoffs]]. In game 1 of the series, Valančiūnas recorded 17 points and 18 rebounds, surpassing [[Keon Clark]]'s franchise record for most rebounds in a single playoff game. He also became the second Raptor ever to record a double-double in his playoff debut; the first was [[Tracy McGrady]].{{cite web |title=Nets claim opener from Raptors as Deron Williams scores 24 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400553085 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=25 June 2020 |date=14 April 2019}} The Raptors went on to lose the series 4–3. ====2014–15 season==== [[File:Jonas the Atlanta Hawks, helping the Raptors record a 50-win season for the first time in franchise history.{{cite web |title=Raptors beat Hawks 105-97 to notch first 50-win season |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400829000 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=25 June 2020 |date=30 March 2016}} On 1 April, he recorded 11 points, 14 rebounds and a career-best seven blocks in a 99–95 win over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite web |title=DeRozan, Lowry lead Raptors past Grizzlies 99-95 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400829019 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=25 June 2020 |date=1 April 2016}} The Raptors finished the regular season as the second seed in the conference with a 56–26 record. During the [[2016 NBA playoffs]], in game 1 of the Raptors' first round playoff series against the seventh-seeded [[Indiana Pacers]], Valančiūnas set a franchise playoff record with 19 rebounds, surpassing his own mark set in 2014.{{cite web |title=Paul George scores 33 as Pacers upend Raptors in Game 1 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400874380 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=25 June 2020 |date=16 June 2016}} In game 2 of the series, Valančiūnas recorded a playoff career-high 23 points and 15 rebounds in a 98–87 win, tying the series a 1–1.{{cite web |title=Jonas Valanciunas has 23 points, 15 boards as Raptors tie series 1-1 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400874381 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=25 June 2020 |date=18 April 2016}} The Raptors went on to win the series 4–3. In the second round, the Raptors faced the [[Miami Heat]], but in game 3 of the series, Valančiūnas went down with a sprained right ankle. He subsequently missed eight straight games, returning to action in game 5 of the Eastern Conference finals against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite web |title=LeBron James, Kevin Love power Cavs to romp over Raptors, 3-2 lead |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400876895 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=25 June 2020 |date=25 May 2016}} The Raptors lost to the Cavaliers in game 6 as the Raptors' deepest playoff run in franchise history ended with a 4–2 series loss.{{cite web |title=Cavs advance to 2nd straight NBA Finals behind LeBron James' 33 points |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400876896 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=25 June 2020 |date=27 May 2016}} ====2016–17 season==== In the Raptors' season opener on 26 October 2016, Valančiūnas recorded a then career-high 32 points and 11 rebounds in a 109–91 win over the Detroit Pistons.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899382|title=DeRozan's 40 leads Raptors to 109-91 win over Pistons|work=ESPN.com|date=26 October 2016|access-date=27 October 2016}}{{cite web|last=Murphy|first=Blake|url=http://www.raptorsrepublic.com/2016/10/26/valanciunas-sets-new-career-high-32-points-opener-derozan-drops-40/|title=Valanciunas sets new career high with 32 points in opener; DeRozan drops 40|work=RaptorsRepublic.com|date=26 October 2016|access-date=27 October 2016}} On 10 January 2017, Valančiūnas grabbed a then career-high 23 rebounds to go with 18 points in a 114–106 win over the [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/raptors-jonas-valanciunas-hauls-in-career-high-23-boards-thursday/|title=Raptors' Jonas Valanciunas: Hauls in career-high 23 boards Thursday|work=CBSSports.com|date=10 January 2017|access-date=9 March 2017}} On 31 March, Valančiūnas made team history in the third quarter of Toronto's 111–100 win over the Indiana Pacers. He had 13 of his 17 rebounds during the quarter, setting a franchise mark for most in a single period. He also had 16 points for his team-leading 28th double-double of the season. He also established a career high during the game, surpassing the 714 rebounds he had in the 2013–14 season.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900521|title=DeRozan powers Raptors past Pacers 111-100|work=ESPN.com|date=31 March 2017|access-date=1 April 2017}} ====2017–18 season==== [[File:Jonas Valanciunas (26715350158).jpg|thumb|right|205px|Valančiūnas with the Toronto Raptors in 2018]]On 11 January 2018, Valančiūnas had 15 points and a season-high 18 rebounds in a 133–99 win over the Cleveland Cavaliers.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975361|title=James, struggling Cavs routed again, Raptors romp 133-99|work=ESPN.com|date=11 January 2018|access-date=26 January 2018}} On 15 January, Valančiūnas was selected as the Lithuanian Basketball Player of the Year for the fourth time.{{cite web |title=Geriausi 2017 metų krepšininkai – Jonas Valančiūnas ir Kamilė Nacickaitė |url=https://www.15min.lt/24sek/naujiena/lietuva/geriausi-2017-uju-metu-krepsininkai-jonas-valanciunas-ir-kamile-nacickaite-875-910674 |website=15min.lt/24sek |access-date=17 August 2025 |language=lt}} On 26 January, he had a season-high 28 points and 14 rebounds in a 97–93 loss to the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975462|title=Rubio's 3 with 4 seconds left lifts Jazz past Raptors 97-93|work=ESPN.com|date=26 January 2018|access-date=26 January 2018}} During the [[2018 NBA playoffs]], in game 2 of the Raptors' first-round playoff series against the [[Washington Wizards]], Valančiūnas had 19 points and 14 rebounds, as Toronto took a 2–0 lead in a playoff series for the first time in franchise history with a 130–119 win. Lithuania went on to win the gold medal and he was chosen as the MVP.{{citation needed|date=June 2020}} In the summer of 2009, Valančiūnas participated in the European Under-18 All-Star Game during [[EuroBasket 2009]]. He dominated the game as he scored 18 points, grabbed 19 rebounds, blocked three shots and helped the "Blue Team" beat the "White Team" 77–75.{{cite web |title=Valanciunas Awarded Champion U18 All Star Game |url=http://www.eurobasket2009.org/en/cid_toT,ovGDH2EaLKL67XnPo2.pageID_z,Bh9EzcJ9AiQ2,78D6YV2.compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2009.roundID_6328.coid_NcyBLnQfIhcd4KGGhsoo22.articleMode_on.html |website=FIBA |access-date=25 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090924032337/http://www.eurobasket2009.org/en/cid_toT%2CovGDH2EaLKL67XnPo2.pageID_z%2CBh9EzcJ9AiQ2%2C78D6YV2.compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2009.roundID_6328.coid_NcyBLnQfIhcd4KGGhsoo22.articleMode_on.html |archive-date=24 September 2009 |date=18 September 2009}} Valančiūnas was later named the MVP of the All-Star game.{{citation needed|date=January 2015}} One year later, Valančiūnas led the [[Lithuania men's national under-18 and under-19 basketball team|Lithuania national under-18 team]] to gold medal. Lithuania dominated in the [[2010 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]]. He averaged 19.4 points, 13.4 rebounds and 2.7 blocks, and was voted as the MVP.{{cite web |title=Simboliniame penketuke – du lietuviai, naudingiausias – Valančiūnas (foto) |url=https://www.basketnews.lt/news-31741-simboliniame-penketuke-du-lietuviai-naudingiausias-valanciunas-foto.html |website=basketnews.lt |access-date=25 June 2020 |language=lt-LT |date=1 August 2010}} [[File:Valančiūnas against Koufos.jpg|thumb|left|Valančiūnas versus [[Kosta Koufos]]]] Valančiūnas was also a member of the Lithuania under-19 team, which competed in the [[2011 FIBA Under-19 World Championship]]. He averaged 15.8 points and 12 rebounds, while leading the tournament in [[double-double]]s and rebounds per game. In 2019, Valančiūnas played the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup]] where Lithuania finished ninth overall. Valančiūnas led his team in total points and rebounds, averaging 14.0 points and 8.8 rebounds. In 2023, Valančiūnas represented the Lithuania at the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup]] where Lithuania finished in sixth place. He averaged 14.8 points, 8.8 rebounds, which included a sensational victory against the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States]]. He became the second player (with [[José Ortiz (basketball)|José Ortiz]]) to have recorded multiple double-doubles in three World Cup tournaments since 1994. In recognition of his individual play, Valančiūnas was named to the [[FIBA Basketball World Cup All-Tournament Team|All-FIBA World Cup Second Team]].{{cite
